paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this chapter. Nehemiah gets a invite, then the same invite four times, then a letter, then a "prophet" with a scary warning. Every one of them was built to pull him off the wall. Nehemiah's answer to the first one tells you everything: "I am doing a great work and cannot come down" (Neh 6:3).

Now watch what he does when the pressure gets personal. The enemies wanted him to hide in the temple and sin, so they could give him "a bad name" (Neh 6:13). Nehemiah says, "Should a man like me run away?" (Neh 6:11), and he sees through it because he realizes God had not sent that man (Neh 6:12). And when the letters try to frighten everybody, he doesn't panic. He prays, "But now, my God, strengthen my hands" (Neh 6:9). That's the move, baker: when the fear shows up, hand it to God and keep working.

And look how it ends. The wall was completed in fifty-two days, and the surrounding nations "realized that this task had been accomplished by our God" (Neh 6:15-16). The enemies never stopped the work, but they sure kept trying, right up to the last verse (Neh 6:19). So whatever God has put in your hands this week, don't let a loud voice talk you down off your wall. Stay on it, ask Him to strengthen your hands, and I'll be right here keeping the oven warm.
